cases.note: _build_parser is the flag inventory, one add_argument per flag with its default and help beside it; splitting it would hide the one table the README's defaults test reads against

main was the scan pipeline in the order it runs, each check followed by its receipt line, and this note argued the length was the number of checks. An external review disagreed, and in 1.6.0 the gathering moved to pipeline.py: the order is still one readable sequence, now of four named stages rather than every statement inline. The finding was real and is closed by the split, not by this note; the record stays because the judgement was made
readiness.assess states the six criteria one Criterion(...) per line on purpose: the list is the specification, and a loop over a table would make it harder to read than the finding it produces
